arm-A.title: The Bug Removed
arm-A.summary: In the moving car, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when suction alone fails to dislodge the tracker, she drives an electric charge through him to force it out; the fluke-like bug rockets through the coils into the glass cage, then reverts to a common wire tap when she tips it out onto the pavement behind the car, which carries on through the rain before halting in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
arm-A.action: Trinity seals the extractor over Neo's navel and increases the suction; when that fails to catch the tracker, she fires an electric charge into him that drives the bug out through the coils into the transparent enclosure at the tubing's far end. She lifts the cage and tips the bug out the window onto the pavement, where it reverts to a common wire tap. The car drives on through the rain and pulls into the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

arm-B.title: The Bug Removed
arm-B.summary: In the car rushing through the rainy night, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when suction alone fails to catch the burrowing tracker, overrides his screams and electrocutes him until the fluke-like bug is driven out through the coils. Neo, who had feared only a wire tap, is stunned into belief when he sees the living thing writhing in the glass cage, and Trinity empties it out into the downpour. The car carries them on through the wet night and comes to a halt in the deserted alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
arm-B.action: Trinity fits the extraction device to Neo's stomach and raises the suction while Switch feeds it power from the cigarette lighter; as the ultrasound monitor shows the tracker burrowing and Switch warns it will be lost, Trinity fires an electric charge through Neo, convulsing him until the bug rockets out into the glass cage, which she then empties out the window. The car drives on through the wet night and stops in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

arm-A.title: Born Into the Real World
arm-A.summary: In cardiac arrest, Neo ruptures the magenta amnion and stands bald and naked in the oval capsule of clear alloy, mirror gel crawling over his face. arm-A.title: The Desert of the Real

Neo resists every step, recoiling from the crew's touch as he comes to see them as agents of an unbearable violation, and when his mind cannot hold the truth his body speaks it — he thrashes against the restraints, tears free of the chair, screams at Trinity, Dozer, and Cypher to get away, then vomits and blacks out on the deck while the crew holds and tends him.
arm-A.action: Morpheus initiates Neo into direct experience of the Matrix and narrates its history and horror while Neo's mind rebels and his body finally gives out.

arm-A.turns_on: The moment Morpheus holds up the coppertop battery and Neo refuses to believe it — the point where revelation stops being information and becomes an assault the mind cannot survive, so the body rejects it instead.

arm-A.boundary_reason: Jacking Neo into the Construct shifts the story to showing him what the Matrix and the real world actually are; Morpheus's history lesson, the fetus-field revelation, and Neo's denial culminate in his physical rejection of the truth and blackout, which ends the revelation sequence.

arm-B.title: The Desert of the Real
arm-B.summary: Morpheus leads Neo off the main deck of the Nebuchadnezzar into the Construct and, rather than defining the Matrix in words, jacks him in and shows him. Across the loading program, the televised history of the scorched sky, the fetus fields, and the power plant, Morpheus lays out how humanity was reduced to a grown power source, holding up a coppertop battery as the final proof. Neo refuses every step of it and demands to be let out; back on the main deck his body rejects what he has been shown, and after the cable is pulled he vomits and collapses unconscious.
arm-B.action: The event converts Neo from being told the truth to being forced to survive it — his intellectual refusal becomes a physical one, ending in blackout.

arm-A.title: After Hours
arm-A.summary: Trinity comes out of NEO'S ROOM having just had a private moment over Neo that she did not mean anyone to witness, and meets Cypher in the HALL, where his needling about her attachment to Neo reads to her as exposure. She keeps her feelings off the record and answers with doctrine, and Cypher, failing to rattle her, pivots to the Oracle as a way to test Morpheus's certainty. Neo stays only the covered, watched object of the exchange, and Trinity walks away on her own terms while Cypher is left armed with a plan rather than a sneer.
arm-A.action: Trinity steps out of NEO'S ROOM and into the HALL, still recovering from the intimate moment she did not intend to be seen, and finds Cypher watching. He jabs that she never brought him dinner and presses that there is something about Neo, then asks why Morpheus does not take Neo to the Oracle, who would know. She treats him as a cynic to be managed, deflects his suspicion by asking if he is a believer and answering that Morpheus will take Neo when he is ready, and turns away, leaving him behind her.

arm-B.title: After Hours
arm-B.summary: Trinity comes out of Neo's room having just been alone with the unconscious Neo in a way she can't own, and runs straight into Cypher watching her; she deflects his needling about her feelings without denying anything and leaves on her own terms, while Cypher—dressing up resentment over the dinner as a joke—fails to rattle her and reaches for the Oracle as a way to force Morpheus's faith into something verifiable, the first step away from loyalty.
arm-B.action: Trinity steps out of Neo's room into the hall, meets Cypher's watch, and turns his suspicion back on him rather than putting anything personal on the record, then walks away and leaves the exchange on her own terms. Over the still, unconscious Neo, Cypher jabs that she never brought him dinner and presses that there is something about Neo; when she deflects instead of denying, he floats routing Neo through the Oracle so Morpheus's certainty can be tested—using the dinner as proof of a favoritism he resents and performing indifference so the probe doesn't look like what it is.
